title: ConditionalHeaderRegexNoOp
description: The story-069 provenance-header injection uses an anchored replace `source.replace(/(\/\/ Updated [^\n]*\n)(?=import)/, ...)`. The pattern only matches when a prior `// Updated` comment line already precedes the import block. If no such line exists, the replace silently no-ops and the provenance/audit-trail header is never injected. The actual address patching is independent and still succeeds; only the provenance header is lost.
impact: Cosmetic / provenance only. The address-patching logic still completes correctly; the sole loss is the audit-trail `// Updated` header when the anchor is absent. No security, correctness, or availability impact on the patched addresses.
evidence: Header injection relies on the regex /(\/\/ Updated [^\n]*\n)(?=import)/ which requires a pre-existing `// Updated` line immediately before `import`.
When no prior `// Updated` line is present, String.replace finds no match and returns the source unchanged (silent no-op).
Address replacement is performed by separate logic and is unaffected by the header no-op.
recommendation: Add an unconditional prepend fallback: when the anchored regex does not match, prepend a fresh `// Updated ...` provenance header before the import block so the audit trail is always written.
